Jordan / Karthik — see Vincere redline. My suggested approach below attempts to balance their security concern with Redwoods need for predictable commercial exposure. Ive attached a one-page summary and a clean clause (Redwood_proposed_language.pdf).

Redwood proposed compromise (summary):
- Carve-out limited to "Willful or intentional unauthorized disclosure of Confidential Information that constitutes a trade secret under applicable law".
- For such events Redwood will: (i) indemnify Customer for third-party claims arising from misappropriation of trade secrets; and (ii) reimburse reasonable and documented costs of investigation, notification and credit monitoring.
- Confirm exclusion remains narrow: does NOT include accidental disclosures caused by Customer misconfiguration, or indirect/consequential damages not reasonably tied to the misappropriation.
- We do NOT accept uncapped general liability; carve-out limited to the narrow trade-secret scenario and reimbursement/indemnity per above.

Draft clause (for insertion into MSA/Order Form):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the liability cap set forth in Section X shall not apply to liability arising from Redwood's willful and intentional unauthorized disclosure or misappropriation of Customer Confidential Information that qualifies as a trade secret under the applicable trade secret statute. In such case Redwood's liability shall be limited to: (a) indemnification for third-party claims directly resulting from such misappropriation; and (b) reasonable, documented costs incurred by Customer for forensic investigation, legal defense, regulatory notification, and credit monitoring. Except as set forth in this paragraph, all other limitations and exclusions of liability remain in effect."

Rationale / risk note: this language is narrower than the customer's initial ask (they wanted "uncapped liability" broadly). Narrowing to willful/intentional conduct and tying to statutory trade secrets significantly reduces open-ended exposure while giving Vincere practical remediation rights. We should expect their counsel to push for broader wording; prepared to negotiate reimbursement caps for forensic/notification costs if they insist.

Attachments: Redwood_proposed_language.pdf (contains clause text + optional deductible language)
